newsitem.title: USA: US to decide soon on more food aid for North Korea.
newsitem.headline: US to decide soon on more food aid for North Korea.

text.p: The U.S. will decide "fairly soon" whether to provide more food aid for North Korea in response to the U.N. World Food Program's latest appeal, an Agency for International Development (AID) aide said Thursday.

Lynn Rogers, acting assistant administrator of AID's Bureau for Humanitarian Response, told Reuters that a fairly quick decision is required because of the six to eight weeks it takes to ship food to North Korea from the U.S.
"You'd probably need to have it there before mid-October" to have the greatest impact, Rogers said.
Rogers declined to say what type of food aid the U.S. could provide, although it has mostly donated corn in the past.
"We might do rice, we might do corn, we might do a corn/rice blend," Rogers said. The U.S. will decide after looking at the specifics of the WFP request, he said.

On Wednesday, the WFP asked donor nations to provide an additional $46 million of food aid for North Korea, which is suffering severe food shortages because of floods in 1995 and 1996 and an highly inefficient farm sector.
In response to an earlier WFP appeal this year for $96 million of food aid for North Korea, the U.S. donated 50,000 tonnes of corn valued at nearly $15 million.
"The reason we chose corn is because we wanted a bulk commodity to provide as much food as possible," Rogers said.
Although rice is a good food for children--the main target of the WFP appeal--it is more expensive than corn, he said.
The last shipment of U.S. corn arrived in North Korea at the end of June. The U.S. has donated $33.4 million of food aid to North Korea over the past two years.
